note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

precepts.text: The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel. The Lord forgave David; he loved David, and David messed up badly. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That does not mean you bunker down into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more. You pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes; it is how you handle the mistake.

note.label: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.why:
“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

precepts.text: David's repentance: I acknowledge my transgressions; against thee only have I sinned; purge me with hyssop and I shall be clean. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways. Get yourself right, then go teach the people that it is good to follow the Lord.
precepts.point: The Lord will never leave off his mercy nor abolish the posterity of his elect. He gave a remnant unto Jacob and out of him a root unto David.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Sirach says of David, “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn't David sin against God? He did. Yet “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned, but David repented, and God took away his sins.

This is how he repented: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.” He confessed.

“Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.” And after he confessed, what did David do? “Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then I'm going to go teach the people.

He teaches them “That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at my example: it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend.

David is a famous man, and he is an example for all of us. Some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere. Much is given and much is required of us as leaders, so we have to be honest, confess, get clean, and then lead the people back to God.

precepts.text: Rehoboam was the foolishness of the people, and Jeroboam showed Ephraim the way of sin.
precepts.point: The prophet Ahijah tore Jeroboam's garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten. God would take ten tribes from Solomon's son and leave one tribe for David's sake.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Solomon fell in love with heathen women, the very nations of which the Lord said “Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods”, and they did. He built a high place for Chemosh for his Moabite wife and for Molech for his Ammonite wife, and did the same for all his strange wives. So the Lord was angry with Solomon, and the prophet Ahijah “rent it in twelve pieces” and told Jeroboam, “Take thee ten pieces”: the kingdom would be rent out of the hand of Solomon’s son, with one tribe left for David’s sake.

Sirach sums up what Solomon left behind him when he died: “Thus rested Solomon with his fathers, and of his seed he left behind him Roboam, even the foolishness of the people, and one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel.” Rehoboam was an idiot. He did not listen to the elders; he listened to the friends he grew up with, and by his counsel he turned the people away.

“There was also Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, and shewed Ephraim the way of sin”. Jeroboam, the mighty man of valor Solomon made ruler over the house of Joseph, plotted against Solomon to rush the prophecy, fled to Egypt, and came back to take the ten tribes. And he showed Ephraim the way of sin.

So the heart Solomon gave to his strange wives bore its fruit in the next generation: a foolish son on the throne of Judah, a king who led Ephraim into sin, and the kingdom divided in two. That is where the dividing hatred between the houses begins.

precepts.text: The countries marvelled at thee for thy songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretation: Sirach says the same thing about Solomon.
precepts.point: He wrote the proverbs and the songs; his wives did not write them.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
“Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Beth–lehemite, that is cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the Lord is with him.” The servant did not say the name, but this son of Jesse who went hard on the instruments was David.

“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

precepts.text: David sung songs with his whole heart and set singers before the altar to daily sing praises; praises in their songs, not filth.
precepts.point: David was also a singer; he praised the Most High with words of glory and sung songs with his whole heart, and he set up the singers before the altar, the same service we read of in 1 Chronicles 25.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
David was also a singer: “In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him. He set singers also before the altar, that by their voices they might make sweet melody, and daily sing praises in their songs.”

That is the same service we read of in 1 Chronicles 25, the singers set before the altar. Praises in their songs, not filth.

precepts.text: David played with lions as with kids and with bears as with lambs; he was a mighty young man, and Saul did not know that about him.
precepts.point: David said, The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. Same God, no difference. And Saul said, Go, and the Lord be with thee.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David gave Saul his resume. Keeping his father’s sheep, when “there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock”, he went out after him and delivered it out of his mouth, “and when he arose against me, I caught him by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.” He might have looked small, but he was killing lions and bears behind his sheep.

“He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.” David was a mighty young man, and Saul did not know that about him.

“The Lord that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.” Same God, no difference. “And Saul said unto David, Go, and the Lord be with thee.”

precepts.text: David slew a giant when he was yet but young and took away reproach from the people; he called upon the Most High, and it was the Most High who gave his right hand strength to slay that mighty warrior.
precepts.point: When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled. They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on; he was in the spirit of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
“Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young? and did he not take away reproach from the people, when he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, and beat down the boasting of Goliath?” David was but a youth, and he took the reproach off of Israel.

Where did the strength come from? “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.” It was the Most High who gave David's right hand its strength.

That is why one shot was all it took. The stone left the sling with the velocity of a bullet, and it “sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.” David “prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone”, and “there was no sword in the hand of David.” He ran, stood upon the Philistine, drew Goliath's own sword “out of the sheath thereof”, and “cut off his head therewith.”

“And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.” They ran from a young youth because they knew something supernatural was going on: he was in the spirit of the Lord.

precepts.text: As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen; he played with lions as with kids and bears as with lambs, and slew a giant when he was young, for he called upon the most high Lord who gave him strength.
precepts.point: The Most High made David's feet like hinds' feet and set him upon high places, and taught his hands to war so that a bow of steel is broken by his arms, not bent but broken. He gave David the shield of his salvation and his gentleness made him great; his repentance enlarged his steps so his feet did not slip. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

note.label: 2 Samuel 22: The Lord Is My Rock and My Fortress

precepts.why:
“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs. Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young?” And “he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.”

That is the man who sang, “He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms.” Not bent, but broken. David knew a lion and a bear were nothing to a man trained by the Most High.

The Most High made David’s feet “like hinds’ feet” and set him upon high places. He gave him “the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great.” His repentance enlarged his steps, “so that my feet did not slip.”

Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” Nathan was the prophet of David’s day, the one through whom the Lord spoke to David.

Solomon reminds Hiram of what the Lord spoke to David his father: “Thy son, whom I will set upon thy throne in thy room, he shall build an house unto my name.” That word came in the time of David, and now Solomon purposes to build the house.

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel. He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs.” He slew a giant “when he was yet but young”, and beat down “the boasting of Goliath”, “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, and set up the horn of his people.”

David was a man of war from his youth. That is why Solomon tells Hiram that “David my father could not build an house unto the name of the Lord his God for the wars which were about him on every side, until the Lord put them under the soles of his feet.”

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“So the people honoured him with ten thousands, and praised him in the blessings of the Lord, in that he gave him a crown of glory. For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his adversaries, and brake their horn in sunder unto this day.”

David destroyed the enemies on every side. Those are the wars that were about him on every side, which kept him from building the house, until the Lord put them “under the soles of his feet.” What David fought through, Solomon inherited as rest.

precepts.point: Solomon asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, for the Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation, and the best cedar came from Lebanon. Lebanon lay to the northwest on the coast, where the best trees grew, and Solomon knew his own people had none who could hew timber like the Zidonians.

note.label: 1 Kings 5: Solomon Makes a League with Hiram to Build the House

precepts.why:
“After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake he dwelt at large. Solomon reigned in a peaceable time, and was honoured; for God made all quiet round about him, that he might build an house in his name, and prepare his sanctuary for ever.”

That is exactly what Solomon tells Hiram: “But now the Lord my God hath given me rest on every side, so that there is neither adversary nor evil occurrent.” God made all quiet round about him so that he might build the house. So Solomon purposes to build it, and asks that cedar trees be hewn out of Lebanon, where the best cedar grew, “for thou knowest that there is not among us any that can skill to hew timber like unto the Sidonians.” The Zidonians had a gift of skill in timber above any other nation.

precepts.text: Look at how David operated: in all his works he praised the Most High with words of glory and loved Him that made him, and even through all the trials he went through the Lord took away his sins and exalted his horn forever. That is what you want, for the Most High to take away your sins.
precepts.point: For thou, Lord, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as with a shield. The Most High fights our battles as long as we align ourselves with these scriptures and keep the commandments, including the commandment of brotherly and sisterly love, which Israel sometimes forgets, especially in marriage. Sometimes you have to take an L in this walk.

note.label: Psalm 5: For Thou Lord Wilt Bless the Righteous

precepts.why:
Look at how David operated. “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.” He “played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs”, and while he was yet young he slew a giant and took away reproach from the people when he “beat down the boasting of Goliath”. How? “For he called upon the most high Lord; and he gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior”. That is the Most High defending the one who put his trust in him, just as Psalm 5 says: “let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them”.

“For he destroyed the enemies on every side, and brought to nought the Philistines his adversaries”. The Most High fights our battles as long as we align ourselves with these scriptures and keep the commandments, including the commandment of brotherly and sisterly love, which Israel sometimes forgets, especially in marriage. Sometimes you have to take an L in this walk.

“In all his works he praised the Holy One most high with words of glory; with his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” He set singers before the altar, beautified the feasts and set in order the solemn times, that the temple might sound from morning. And through all the trials he went through, “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” That is what you want: for the Most High to take away your sins. That is how he blesses the righteous and compasses him with favour as with a shield.
